findings: [HIGH][DBML-IDENTIFIER][docs/database/v1-scheme.dbml:party_identifiers.normalized_value_hash] The canonical textual encoding and case of the HMAC-SHA-256 fingerprint are not defined or constrained. Evidence: the field is CHAR(64) and described only as hexadecimal at docs/database/v1-scheme.dbml:295, while the unconditional case-sensitive unique key is declared at lines 313-315 and permanent uniqueness is required by requirements-amendment-001.md:35-61. Impact: alternate textual representations of the same fingerprint, including case differences, could bypass the persistence-owned permanent uniqueness boundary.

[MEDIUM][DBML-QUALITY][docs/database/v1-scheme.dbml:parties.display_name] The denormalized display_name is required to be maintained atomically with the corresponding detail row, but its authoritative derivation and normalization rules for natural persons and legal entities are absent. Evidence: docs/database/v1-scheme.dbml:109 and 128-134; no approved requirement or architecture rule defines whether preferred names, given/family-name ordering, legal names, or trade names control the value. Impact: downstream implementation would have to invent business-visible search and presentation behavior and could persist inconsistent denormalized data.

[MEDIUM][DBML-MIGRATION][docs/database/v1-scheme.dbml:natural_person_details.Note, party_nationalities.Note, party_identifiers.Note] PostgreSQL obligations that DBML cannot express are not migration-deterministic. Evidence: lines 157-164 require a deferred constraint trigger without its object name, covered operations, or exact timing; lines 218-226 require two partial unique indexes without names or exact predicates and refer to tenant scope although party_nationalities has no tenant_id; lines 328-350 require another partial unique index without a name or explicit migration-test obligation. Impact: independent Flyway implementations could create materially different integrity mechanisms or omit required behavior.
